title: Decomposition, reusable functions and interface contracts (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Break a larger task into functions with focused responsibilities.
Define preconditions, postconditions and side effects for each function.
Choose parameter and return types that express the function's contract.
Handle errors consistently and document ownership rules.
Test functions independently and test their integration.

understand.concept: Program decomposition separates a larger task into functions with clear responsibilities. An interface contract states valid inputs, outputs, side effects and error behavior. A reliable function also makes pointer ownership and object lifetime expectations explicit. Good decomposition reduces duplication while keeping each function understandable and testable.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit contracts make functions easier to test, reuse and maintain. They also reduce hidden assumptions between callers and callees.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Decompose by responsibility

Separate input, validation, calculation, storage and presentation when those tasks have distinct responsibilities. Avoid both one enormous function and excessive fragmentation into meaningless helpers.

## 2. Define the contract

Document preconditions, postconditions, side effects and failure behavior. State whether pointer parameters may be null and whether the function borrows or owns pointed-to storage.

## 3. Design the interface

Use parameter types that communicate what the function needs. Use const-qualified pointers for read-only access and return values or output parameters to communicate results.

## 4. Handle errors predictably

Choose a consistent error strategy: status return values, documented sentinel values or another explicit interface. Do not silently return plausible but incorrect data after a failure.

## 5. Test at two levels

Test each function against its contract, then test the composition of functions in the complete program. Boundary and failure tests are part of the contract, not optional extras.

practise.guidedTask: Implement a focused C program demonstrating CL6.10. State the function's inputs, output, preconditions and failure behavior before coding.
